name: nested_bayesian_evidence
description: Fully nested Bayesian evidence computation for TEP vs explicit astrophysical alternatives, using both multi-observable joint tests (primary) and single-observable supplementary tests.

observable_covariance.note: Empirical covariance of standardized observables used in the joint covariance likelihood.  The off-diagonal elements quantify the SED-output correlations that the independent-likelihood models double-count.

preprocessing.note: Observables and log(Gamma_t) were z-scored before nested sampling so the shared Gaussian-noise priors are valid across domains with very different scales. In the joint test, mass and z are orthogonalized against log(Gamma_t) before being used as predictors in the alternative models, preventing the alternatives from absorbing the TEP signal through the raw mass variable. Non-linear terms (burst, AGN sigmoid) retain raw mass for physical interpretability. TEP-corrected alternatives use M_true = M_obs - n*log10(Gamma_t) where n = 0.7, and corrected sSFR = sSFR_obs + n*log10(Gamma_t), to test whether the TEP mass correction improves the fit of standard astrophysical models.

physical_subset_summary.note: Excludes SED chi2 (fitting diagnostic, not physical observable). This is the conservative headline result.

key_finding.statement: Multi-observable joint nested Bayesian model comparison decisively favours TEP over all tested alternatives. Mean ln(BF) across 11 alternatives = 123.9 (log10 = 53.8).  TEP achieves this with the fewest parameters, leveraging a single theory-fixed predictor (Gamma_t) across all observables.
key_finding.methodology: Dynesty nested sampling with nlive=200, dlogz=0.5, multi-observable joint likelihood across 4 observables (dust, log_ssfr, chi2, met).  TEP uses 12 params (3 per observable, shared log(Gamma_t) predictor) while alternatives range from 16 to 28 params.

residual_space_key_finding.statement: Residual-space nested Bayesian comparison decisively favours TEP over all tested residual alternatives. After removing linear mass+z trends from both observables and competing predictors, mean ln(BF) across 2 alternatives = 128.9 (log10 = 56.0).
residual_space_key_finding.methodology: Residual-space dynesty comparison with nlive=200, dlogz=0.5. Observables and competing predictors were residualized against the orthogonalized design [1, mass_ortho, z_ortho] — the components of mass and z orthogonal to log R_ML — so this family is TEP-conditioned: the R_ML-aligned direction is retained in both the data and the TEP predictor by construction. The symmetric counterpart residualized against raw [1, log_Mstar, z] is reported separately as the conventional residual-space comparison. Residual TEP uses 12 params, residual null uses 8, and constrained AGN uses 10 params with metallicity excluded from explicit AGN contamination response.

correction_summary.verdict: TEP mass correction does not improve astrophysical model fits

correction_key_finding.statement: Applying the TEP mass correction (M_true = M_obs - 0.7*log10(Gamma_t)) does not improve astrophysical model fits (3/4 models worsened, mean ln(BF) = -3.1), suggesting the TEP mass correction does not recover the true physical driver.  Per-model results: Standard_Physics: ln(BF)=-7.9; Bursty_SF: ln(BF)=-8.6; Varying_IMF: ln(BF)=7.0; AGN_Feedback: ln(BF)=-2.8.
correction_key_finding.methodology: Each astrophysical alternative was run with both observed mass (M_obs) and TEP-corrected mass (M_true = M_obs - 0.7*log10(Gamma_t)).  Same parameter counts ensure the comparison isolates the effect of the TEP mass correction. Positive ln(BF) means the correction improves the fit, supporting TEP as a measurement correction framework.
